subject.title: fix(agents): classify Anthropic refusal and OpenAI content_filter as failover-eligible refusals

question: Should OpenClaw accept a default-off generic refusal fallback policy for provider safety/content-filter refusals?
rationale: Even with the safe default, the new config creates an operator-controlled path that can send a provider-blocked prompt to another model or provider with different safety behavior.

options.title: Accept after consistency fixes
options.body: Allow the config surface once every fallback entry point honors it, sibling transports classify refusals consistently, and real gateway/provider proof is posted.

options.title: Keep generic fallback out
options.body: Rely on provider-sanctioned fallback paths such as Anthropic Fable-to-Opus and keep generic/OpenAI refusals terminal until a narrower policy is designed.

options.title: Ship diagnostics only
options.body: Improve refusal diagnostics and user copy without automatic model fallback until the cross-provider security policy is settled.

recommendation.title: Accept after consistency fixes
recommendation.body: Allow the config surface once every fallback entry point honors it, sibling transports classify refusals consistently, and real gateway/provider proof is posted.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the merged provider-side Anthropic fallback and has the closest recent policy context for the remaining generic refusal fallback question.
